experiment: batch-generation scaling for the full entity-coverage run
scope: CPU batch preparation only; no model/optimizer step in the scaling runs. One prepared-batch pickle measurement and synthetic 46 ms consumer for overlap tests.

interpretation.loading_dataset_into_gestaltdb_ram: No measurable gain. Resident CSR 126.2 ms vs mmap 127.7 ms; the CSR is already in the page cache and the cost is CPU frontier/feature construction.
interpretation.gestaltdb_engine_sampling: Not used: SamplerEngine.sample_subgraph/sample_layers are per-node Python loops and do not implement the custom supervised-positive masking. The useful GestaltDB pieces are CSRAdjacency/build_csr, AsyncBatchFeeder and worker_engine.
interpretation.thread_overlap: A background producer hides much of the 46 ms GPU update: 173.6 -> 137.2 ms (1.27x) with prefetch 2, 131.3 ms (1.32x) with prefetch 4.
interpretation.process_scaling: Generation scales to 14.9/25.3/37.7 batches/s with 2/4/8 forked workers. Four workers already exceed the 21.7 updates/s GPU ceiling at this batch size.
interpretation.ipc: A prepared batch pickles to 31.4 MiB. A real multi-process pipeline must either pay ~11 ms dump + ~1.8 ms load per batch or use shared memory; the measured pool numbers exclude IPC and TensorFlow conversion.
interpretation.projected_end_to_end: Not measured. Thread prefetch projects to about 7.3-7.6 updates/s. A 4-worker producer pool, if IPC is kept below the 46 ms update, projects to roughly 15-18 updates/s. These are projections, not completed training results.

caveats: Benchmark ran while the real trainer was active; wall-clock rates include normal CPU contention.
Each worker used an independent deterministic RNG derived from (seed, step); this is not the live sequential RNG stream.
Generation-only measurements exclude tensor conversion, gradient updates, validation, checkpoint writes and export.
RAM-vs-mmap test copied the 2.2 GB CSR into resident arrays; the comparison is warm-cache, not cold-start.
No held-out metrics were used to choose these settings.
